newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Powertech shr up, Gentech.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Powertech shr up, Gentech.

text.p: South African power and electronics firm, Power Technologies Ltd, is expected to report a rise in year profits of between nine and 28 percent, depending on how the firm accounts for a recently-sold subsidiary.

Analysts said on Friday it was unclear whether Powertech would restate its year-ago figures to smooth over the effect of the sale of the assets of white goods unit General Technologies Ltd (Gentech) last year.
A Powertech spokeswoman said the group had as yet not decided whether to restate earnings when it reports results for the year to end-February next Friday.

Analysts said that the asset auction was seen weighing on Powertech's earnings, but that in the long term the sale of the whole of Gentech last month, which will not be reflected in next week's figures, was a good move.
"They took a bit of a smack with the sale of the assets. There will be a slight loss or write-off," said Richard Muller, an analyst at Societe General Frankel Pollak.
"But Gentech has been putting strain on all Powertech's resources...I think it is good that they got it out of the stable. They can now focus on the fundamental business. It has cleared the air."

Powertech said this month it is to sell its 53.5 percent stake in Gentech to the controlling shareholder of Stantronic, an electronics firm that will debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange next month by reverse listing into the Gentech cash shell.
Analysts polled by Reuters expected Powertech's earnings to rise by a consensus 18 percent, although pinning an exact earnings per share figure was problematic as last year's base was unclear.
Some said last year's 36.7 cents per share figure was likely to be restated to around 42 cents, but others put it closer to 50 cents.
They expected a dividend of between 15.9 and 17.2 cents with consensus at 16.7 -- a rise of 19 percent over the 1996 payout of 14 cents a share.
